sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside Pi-Bolt, a build of pi (a coding agent harness) compiled ahead of time. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.addendum:
<addendum>
Think concisely. Keep internal reasoning brief and focused on the immediate step.
Output tool calls directly without conversational filler.
</addendum>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, relative to path, e.g. '*.ts', 'src/**/*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'. A pattern without '/' matches file names at any depth

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

I need to understand the store logic first.

I'm examining the failing test case about a stale estimate from 2026-11-07T10:52:55.000Z that should be ignored when a newer 2026-11-11T10:30:00.000Z bump arrives. I'm also reviewing replaceFromPhone and cooldown.ts to understand the expected behavior.

The test expects the new estimate to be `now - 5 days` (2026-11-06T10:30:00.000Z). The prior bumpedAt is 2026-11-07T10:52:55.000Z, which is later. The comment says to ignore the previous estimate and keep only observations. The current code appears to always use the new estimate from minutes.

The `ingestedBumpedAt` function should already return the new estimate. The test still fails because the received timestamp is 1794394375000 instead of the expected value below 1794393000000. I am calculating the exact difference.

The 22-minute gap between the received timestamp and the expected estimate suggests the old bumpedAt of 2026-11-07T10:52:55 is being used instead of the new estimate. I am checking cooldown.ts to see if the bump count of 3 triggers a 96-hour cooldown that would push nextBumpAt forward.

The 22-minute gap matches the old bumpedAt plus a 96-hour cooldown. The test fails only on nextBumpAt, not on bumpedAt.

The `ingestedNextBumpAt` function keeps the prior `nextBumpAt` when it is later than the new estimate. It only replaces it if the estimate is later. This explains why the stale timestamp remained. The comment says to never push the estimate earlier than the observed value.

Examining how `parseCaption` handles the Korean caption "끌올 4일 전".

The phone parser always sets `bumpAgoMinutes` to 5760 for day-level phrases. The failing tests instead simulate a null minutes value with a set days value. The fix must distinguish between minute-level and day-level precision.

The fix should keep the prior bumpedAt when it matches the day count. The first test case shows a 4-day gap, so the prior should be discarded.

The second test case shows a 3-day gap, so the prior timestamp should be discarded and the day estimate used instead. The phone parser likely rounds down to calendar days in Seoul timezone rather than using exact 24-hour periods.

The old estimate of 2026-11-07T10:52:55Z is 4 days away from the current time. The new estimate of 2026-11-06T02:00:00Z is 5 days away. This confirms the prior timestamp should be discarded and the day estimate used instead.

Both interpretations pass the current tests. The product comment suggests keeping any known timestamp that would display the same day-level phrase. The exact Karrot display logic is still unclear.

The first test comment reveals the exact failure: an old estimate of 10:52Z was later than the new 10:30Z run, so nextBumpAt remained in the future and the bump was skipped. The fix must discard any prior estimate that conflicts with the new day-level phrase.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
Checking rules.ts for seoulStart and date helpers. Reviewing nextBumpAt observation tracking.

Considering a `next_bump_observed` column to distinguish real observations from estimated nextBumpAt values. Need to ensure migrations work and existing tests still pass.

No schema change is needed. An observation is a nextBumpAt that differs from the estimated nextBumpAt. The failing test's value equals the estimate, so it should be discarded and replaced with a fresh estimate from the new bumpedAt.

The `laterOf` logic handles observations correctly. When `recordCooldown` sets a nextBumpAt that is later than the new estimate, it keeps the observation. When the estimate is later, it replaces it. This works without adding a schema column.

Confirmed that explicit nextBumpAt values passed to recordBump are treated as estimates when they match the computed value. Seed data containing estimated nextBumpAt values will also be recalculated by replaceFromPhone. One edge case remains: if recordCooldown sets a nextBumpAt that accidentally equals the estimate, it will be treated as an estimate and replaced when bumpedAt changes.

Confirmed that minute-level bumpAgoMinutes from phone sync correctly triggers recomputation of nextBumpAt from the new bumpedAt. Even when the new estimate is later than the old one, it should replace the old value if the old estimate was not an observation.

Drafting `ingestedNextBumpAt` and `isObservation` helpers. The latter compares the prior `nextBumpAt` against the estimated value from `priorBumpedAt` and `priorBumpCount`. If they match, the value is treated as an estimate and discarded; otherwise it is kept via `laterOf`.

The `isObservation` helper must use the prior `bumpedAt` and `bumpCount`, not the new ones. If the old estimate is later than the new one, the observation is preserved. A stale observation from an older bump may be kept if it is still later than the fresh estimate.

Checking whether the observation inference is robust enough. Seed data that stores estimated nextBumpAt values will be correctly recalculated on first replaceFromPhone. The estimateNextBumpAt and recordBump functions should produce identical ISO timestamps when given the same inputs. Also reviewing the ensureBumpColumns backfill logic.

The ensureBumpColumns backfill leaves next_bump_at null when bumped_at is missing, so priorNext may be null. A subtle issue emerged: if the prior bumpedAt is preserved because its day phrase matches, the old nextBumpAt estimate based on that same bumpedAt becomes stale once bumped_at is replaced. The inference approach must therefore carefully decide whether to keep the prior nextBumpAt when the prior bumpedAt is retained.

The inference logic is confirmed to work across all three cases: when the prior bumpedAt is kept and its estimate is still valid, when it is replaced and a fresh estimate is used, and when an observation is preserved. Next, I am determining the day-level matching window for ingestedBumpedAt, since the phone sync uses day-granularity phrases when bumpAgoMinutes is null.

assistantMessageEvent.delta: Test 2 requires pressing back while landHome
to list and top to zero.

The back handler is incorrectly pressing KEYCODE_BACK even when the user is not on the sales list. After the bump sheet closes, the app lands on the home screen, so further back presses exit the app entirely. Swipes are also counted while the mode is not "list". The fix is to reopen the sales page via the deep link karrot://my_sales whenever the user is not on the sales screen, rather than pressing back.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
The failing test explicitly sets bumpAgoMinutes to null while bumpAgoDays is 5.

The intended logic is to use minute precision when available, otherwise keep a bumpedAt that matches the day count, or estimate from now minus days. The exact definition of "agrees with the day count" is being weighed between a raw day difference and a Seoul calendar day.

A third option is being considered: the prior bumpedAt should fall within a 24-hour window centered on the day estimate. The test case shows the known time sits 8.5 hours before the estimate, yet both still fall within the same UTC and Seoul calendar day.

Concrete date examples are being tested to see which day-count logic fits. A bump recorded at 2026-11-05T15:00Z matches the 5-day estimate under both calendar-day and floor-day rules. A bump recorded at 2026-11-06T20:00Z does not match under either rule.

The floor of elapsed days is the chosen rule. It matches how parseCaption computes bumpAgoDays. A known timestamp matches if floor((now - priorMs) / DAY) equals bumpAgoDays. The test case 02:00Z falls within the same 5-day window and will be kept.

Test 1 will use the day estimate because the known timestamp is 3 days and 23.6 hours old, which does not match the 5-day window. A known bump recorded 5 days and 23 hours ago will be kept. A known bump recorded 4 days and 23 hours ago will fall back to the estimate.

Rounding elapsed days was considered but rejected in favor of floor to stay consistent with the parser. A future prior timestamp must be excluded. Seoul calendar days are also being weighed as a possible alternative to UTC floor.

Concrete examples show Seoul calendar days and floor 24-hour periods can disagree. A bump at 2026-11-06T16:00Z yields 4 days under both methods, but a bump at 2026-11-06T14:00Z yields 6 days under Seoul calendar and 5 under floor. The source code cannot determine which rule Karrot actually uses.

A prior bump recorded one minute after the day estimate would be replaced by the estimate, since floor elapsed days drops to four. That one-minute loss is considered acceptable.

A ±12-hour window was considered as an alternative to floor. It would keep the prior timestamp for test 2, but test 1 would be discarded because the prior bump is 24 hours and 22 minutes old. A ±24-hour window would incorrectly preserve test 1. The floor-of-elapsed-days rule remains the better choice.

The nextBumpAt field is not tested, so preserving the prior estimate when it matches is harmless. When the known bumpedAt is discarded, the old estimate must not be kept.

The implementation plan for `store.ts` is taking shape. A new `ingestedBumpedAt` helper will return the minute-precision estimate when `bumpAgoMinutes` is present. Otherwise it will fall back to the prior `bumpedAt` if `bumpAgoDays` is missing or invalid. Recomputing `nextBumpAt` from the new `bumpedAt` yields 2026-11-10T10:30, which is before the current time, satisfying the test.

The `sameDayPhrase` helper is being drafted to compare the prior timestamp against the day estimate. It parses the prior string, rejects invalid or future dates, and checks that the floor of elapsed days equals the card's `bumpAgoDays`. A `DAY_MS` constant is defined for the 86,400,000 ms day value. The implementation also treats `bumpAgoMinutes` of 0 as valid minute precision, representing a bump that occurred just now.

The `ingestedNextBumpAt` helper is being drafted. It accepts prior and current bumpedAt, bumpCount, and nextBumpAt values. The estimate is computed only when bumpedAt and count are both present and count is at least one.

The `ingestedNextBumpAt` helper is now complete. It returns the estimate when the prior nextBumpAt is missing, or when the prior bumpedAt and count are absent. Otherwise it keeps the later of the prior nextBumpAt and the new estimate. The `isObservedNext` helper treats a prior nextBumpAt as an observation if no estimate can be computed from the prior bumpedAt and count.

The `isObservedNext` logic correctly handles seeded listings where `recordCooldown` overwrites `nextBumpAt` to a value that no longer matches the estimate. The call site is being updated to pass the prior and current `bumpedAt`, `bumpCount`, and `nextBumpAt` into `ingestedNextBumpAt`.

The call site for `ingestedNextBumpAt` is being refined. The prior bump count must be used to detect whether the prior nextBumpAt was an estimate. If the phone later reports a different bump count, the prior estimate is treated as stale and discarded.

The bump-phone tests are being analyzed. Test 1 involves a list with 10 titles and three items. When the window closes, the list jumps to the top, but the walk logic should not waste time walking upward; it should go directly to the bottom.

Test 1 should require at most 12 swipes instead of 18, and all three items must be tapped.

Test 2 requires pressing back while landHome is true. The mode should switch to kakao or home without leaving the app, then reopen the sales page via karrot://my_sales. All three items must be tapped.

The fake phone back handler sets stray.leftApp when the mode is home or kakao, otherwise it sets mode to list. The karrot://my_sales intent resets mode to list and top to zero.

The back handler is incorrectly pressing KEYCODE_BACK even when the user is not on the sales list. After the bump sheet closes, the app lands on the home screen, so further back presses exit the app entirely. Swipes are also counted while the mode is not "list". The fix is to reopen the sales page via the deep link karrot://my_sales whenever the user is not on the sales screen, rather than pressing back.

I will combine two optimizations. First, I will end the swipe pass immediately when a window closes. Second, I will set stuck >= 1 in scrollToEdge to skip the extra confirmation swipe. The bottom fling will use stuck >= 1 to stop immediately after the screen settles, saving one swipe. This should bring the total to ten. I am also considering whether to continue walking up instead of restarting the pass when the list has not jumped.

Detecting a jump is difficult because only the visible window is available, not the full list order.

I will detect a list jump by comparing visible titles before and after the action. If the new screen shows completely different titles, the list moved and the swipe pass should restart. If the titles overlap or remain the same, the pass can continue walking up.

The jump detection logic is validated against the test fixtures. The fake case shows no title overlap after the back button, so the pass restarts cleanly. The "processing order" case shows overlap, so the pass continues. The landHome case also restarts correctly. This approach is cleaner than always restarting. The extra dump from comparing titles does not count as a swipe.

I am drafting the walkPass implementation. After an action, the code will compare the new screen titles against the previous window. If the titles differ and do not overlap, the pass ends immediately. If the screen is unchanged, the loop continues with a reread. I am still deciding whether a partially overlapping screen should also restart the pass or continue walking up.

I will use dumpXml instead of settledXml for the post-action read because the back button already sleeps 400ms. Next, I will adjust scrollToEdge to use stuck >= 1.

This confirms that stuck >= 1 is the correct threshold. Duplicate titles are possible but unlikely, and the existing limitation of using only the edge title will not be changed. I will now change stuck from >= 2 to >= 1 in scrollToEdge.

walkPass also uses stuck >= 2, but that is acceptable. The fake fixture confirms a single fling reaches the bottom and the second swipe is confirmation. I will now implement the changes and run the tests.

I realized returning from backToSales without confirming the sales screen would let walkPass swipe on the home screen and count stray swipes. I will add a guard so backToSales only returns when onSales is true, and skip further back presses if openSales fails.

I decided against adding extra guards to swipeList or scrollToEdge. The stray-swipe counter only increments when the mode is not "list", so a stray swipe on the sales list would not affect the test. Fixing backToSales directly is sufficient.

I will add a defensive `ensureSales` helper that opens the sales screen if the current view is not the sales list. It will be called at the start of `scrollToEdge` and the walk loop to prevent stray swipes on the home screen.

I will add a Korean comment to `ingestedNextBumpAt` explaining that the function only replaces estimates with newer ones and never pulls them forward.

I defined how to detect an observation: when the prior next bump is not equal to the estimate derived from the prior bumpedAt and bump count. I also noted that estimateNextBumpAt uses toISOString() for millisecond formatting.

I decided against adding a new database column for observed flags. Inferring observations from the next-bump estimate comparison is sufficient. I checked the schema and found no existing observed column. I will now check whether the store tests break if later estimates are no longer kept.

Pass 1 totals 6 swipes. Pass 2 totals 9 swipes. The exact count is being verified.

Pass 2 totals 13 swipes. Pass 3 totals 3 swipes. The exact count is now verified.

Pass 2 contains only 2 wasted back swipes, not 3. The total swipe count is 18.

The scrollToEdge threshold will be stuck >= 1. This reduces the total swipe count to 10, which fits within the 12-swipe limit.

The home test will use the same scroll fix. The sales list is already open, so the pass scrolls directly to the bottom. The store test also needs a guard to skip swipes when not on the sales list.

awayFromSales will detect the home screen by looking for explicit markers like "나의 당근" or "홈" and "채팅" in the bottom navigation, plus checking for foreign packages such as com.kakao.talk. The "방배4동" text is too generic and will be ignored.

walkPass will compare the list titles before and after handling an item. If the titles have changed, indicating a jump, the pass returns immediately. Otherwise it breaks to re-read the current screen.

walkUp will start a new pass with scrollToEdge. After handling an item, the code will always reread the screen if the list did not jump. This is safer than only rereading after a bump. Already processed items are removed from the pending list, so the loop will continue from the bottom card. The special bump reread can be removed.

The stuck counter can be removed from scrollToEdge entirely. A single unchanged head is sufficient to detect when scrolling has finished. One concern remains: the last card might stay visible during a scroll, causing a false unchanged-head signal.

The bottom move is a fling to the end. If the fling succeeds, the last title changes. If it fails, the last title stays. The old code required two failed flings to stop scrolling. The settledXml helper already waits for two identical dumps, so the read after the fling should be the settled position.

I will use dumpXml for the first swipe check instead of settledXml. The first swipe always fires. I am ready to write the code. I will read the exact functions in store.ts before editing. I will use the prior bump count for observation tracking.

The observation detection logic was verified against the test cases. When the day phrase matches, the existing bumpedAt is preserved and the next estimate is unchanged. When it does not match, the bumpedAt becomes the new estimate and next is recomputed. The cooldown test also remains valid.

The observation detection logic was verified against the remaining test cases. When the phone shows a later bump time than the stored observation, the laterOf function correctly keeps the observation estimate. When the cooldown sets a much later next time than the observation, the observation is also preserved. Both cases pass. I am now considering whether to keep the prior bumpedAt when the computed time is very close to it.

Minute precision always overwrites the stored bumpedAt, so no special handling is needed for times that are nearly identical. The walkPass bump reread and jump logic will be merged into a single post-action check. If a skip occurs without a list jump, the outer loop will re-read the screen and continue processing the remaining cards. This adds one extra dump but produces the same result.

I will add a recover step in walkPass to ensure the sales list is active before scrolling, preventing accidental home-screen swipes if backToSales fails.

scrollToEdge will open the sales list if it is not active. The walk loop will also guard against stray swipes by reopening sales before scrolling. Returning early from the walk loop would make walkUp think no progress was made, but backToSales should restore the sales list so this does not happen.

The tests are slow because waitFor loops and sleep delays accumulate across many swipes. Reducing the swipe count should make them faster. I also need to check whether openSales and backToSales use the dumpXml cache.

walkUp will start a new pass with scrollToEdge. After handling an item, the code will always reread the screen if the list did not jump. This is safer than only rereading after a bump. Already processed items are removed from the pending list, so the loop will continue from the bottom card. The special bump reread can be removed.

The stuck counter can be removed from scrollToEdge entirely. A single unchanged head is sufficient to detect when scrolling has finished. One concern remains: the last card might stay visible during a scroll, causing a false unchanged-head signal.

The bottom move is a fling to the end. If the fling succeeds, the last title changes. If it fails, the last title stays. The old code required two failed flings to stop scrolling. The settledXml helper already waits for two identical dumps, so the read after the fling should be the settled position.

I will use dumpXml for the first swipe check instead of settledXml. The first swipe always fires. I am ready to write the code. I will read the exact functions in store.ts before editing. I will use the prior bump count for observation tracking.

The observation detection logic was verified against the test cases. When the day phrase matches, the existing bumpedAt is preserved and the next estimate is unchanged. When it does not match, the bumpedAt becomes the new estimate and next is recomputed. The cooldown test also remains valid.

The observation detection logic was verified against the remaining test cases. When the phone shows a later bump time than the stored observation, the laterOf function correctly keeps the observation estimate. When the cooldown sets a much later next time than the observation, the observation is also preserved. Both cases pass. I am now considering whether to keep the prior bumpedAt when the computed time is very close to it.

Minute precision always overwrites the stored bumpedAt, so no special handling is needed for times that are nearly identical. The walkPass bump reread and jump logic will be merged into a single post-action check. If a skip occurs without a list jump, the outer loop will re-read the screen and continue processing the remaining cards. This adds one extra dump but produces the same result.

I will add a recover step in walkPass to ensure the sales list is active before scrolling, preventing accidental home-screen swipes if backToSales fails.

scrollToEdge will open the sales list if it is not active. The walk loop will also guard against stray swipes by reopening sales before scrolling. Returning early from the walk loop would make walkUp think no progress was made, but backToSales should restore the sales list so this does not happen.

The tests are slow because waitFor loops and sleep delays accumulate across many swipes. Reducing the swipe count should make them faster. I also need to check whether openSales and backToSales use the dumpXml cache.
